topPick.label: Professional Services × 50–199 × Core Corporate (S$2,000–S$2,999)
rationale: 1,135 modeled accounts — the largest modeled 50–199 pool among the high-laptop-intensity target hypotheses.
High laptop intensity: predominantly knowledge-work roles rather than a frontline-heavy workforce.
Dominant bulk hypothesis is mainstream business computing — the Core Corporate S$2,000–S$2,999 cluster is the primary battlefield.
Premium Mobile (S$3,000–S$3,999) is a secondary role-based opportunity inside the same accounts, not the whole fleet.
The < S$2,000 price-led fleet is a negative/tactical filter — if the real standard fleet is mainly sub-S$2,000, this target falls.

whatWouldChangeThisAnswer: Current #1 falls if the actual standard fleet in Professional Services × 50–199 is mainly sub-S$2,000 and price-led.
Current #1 strengthens if the normal standard fleet is around S$2,000–S$2,999 and refreshes in meaningful batches.
Premium Mobile rises if firms have a visible mobile/senior-user tier around S$3,000–S$3,999.
Finance & Insurance rises if the brand clears enterprise security/manageability/warranty requirements.
Information & Communications falls if a large share of relevant users needs NVIDIA/CUDA/workstation-class graphics.
